text:
devin-runtime: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime bump that changes kernel selection, we started seeing a steady 20-35% p99 token latency increase on the 8k sequences in prod canary. nsys traces point to repeated KV read stalls inside the fused-flash variant.
kai-profiling: ugh, saw that on the perf dashboard this morning. Can you attach an nsys snapshot? suspect the prefetch window isn't covering our slice size so we get a lot of SM-migrations.
sara-engr: pinging the canary instance logs + trace: https://perf.example.com/trace/2001abc — the timeline shows small bursts of L2 miss storms right before the stall spikes.
maria-ml: quick notes: this only reproduces with batch_size >= 16 and seq_len >= 4096. On H100 it's milder. A100 is the worst.
devin-runtime: attached nsys capture: `nsys profile -o /tmp/200123 -t cuda,osrt,cuda_mem_sync --trace-fork --sample=none --cpuctx-events` and perfetto link above. Key snippet: repeated kernels named `fused_flash_attn_kv_read` with high stalled cycles.
kai-profiling: pasted flame: `GPU Stalls: 42%` on that kernel. Also saw warp_serialize & bank_conflict counters spike. nvprof counters: `gld_transactions` high and `shared_load_transactions` low => prefetch missing or serialized.
sara-engr: here's the short repro command we used locally: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 python -m benchmarks.attn_kv --model gpt-like --seq 8192 --batch 16 --variant fused-flash --prefetch 4` — increasing prefetch to 12 reduces stalls but latency still worse than old kernel.
maria-ml: hypothesis: the kernel-selection heuristic recently started preferring fused-flash for medium seqs because of average throughput wins, but it doesn't account for interleaved KV read/write patterns produced by our continuous-batching logic (prefix caching). The prefetch window needs to be aligned with slice boundaries.
devin-runtime: agreed. I think the selection threshold is only based on seq_len and peak_tokens. We should add a metric for recent KV-read contention and per-slice latency variance. Also maybe a fallback to the separate-kernel path when bank_conflict rate > X.
kai-profiling: quick experiment: forced kernel to `separated_kv_attn` in runtime config and re-ran the trace. p99 down by 28%, throughput slightly lower but much more stable. logs: `prefetch_lookahead=6` vs fused default of `4`.
perf-bot: deploybot: canary deploy 2026-03-17T08:14 succeeded for cluster-gamma :rocket:
sara-engr: What about batching heuristics? Continuous batching creates many small KV reads that collide. Maybe cap per-request slice merging so fused kernel doesn't get interleaved read/write waves.
devin-runtime: good idea. Proposed mitigations (quick list):
- revert kernel-selection change for seq >= 4096 until we add contention metrics
- increase default prefetch for fused-flash to 10 for A100 profiles
- add a sampler that measures bank_conflict_rate over sliding window and feed to selector
- add a canary config that forces `separated` for 2% of traffic to validate at scale
maria-ml: i'll run a broader matrix (batch: 8/16/32 x seq: 2048/4096/8192 x prefetch: 4/8/12) on both H100/A100 and produce heatmaps. Expecting tradeoff surface where fused wins for throughput but separated for p99.
kai-profiling: FYI here's a small perf command I used to collect counters: `nsys profile --sample=no --trace=cuda --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --export=sqlite -o /tmp/run; ncu --target-processes all --metrics gld_throughput,shared_load_transactions,bank_conflict -o /tmp/ncu`.
devin-runtime: thanks — Kai, can you push a tiny selector patch that reads `bank_conflict_rate` and thresholds at 0.15? we'll run internal perf tests. I'll also add logs in the selector so we can see reasons in the console.
perf-bot: perf-alert: A100 nightly sweep shows regression while fused-flash is default for seq>=4096 (regression detected: +22% p99). See job 200123-nightly.
sara-engr: also note: quantized model variant flips memory layout for KV so fused prefetching pattern changes. We should include model-layout in heuristic keys.
maria-ml: adding to matrix. I'll attach CSV when done. Expect initial results in ~3 hours.
kai-profiling: quick question — do we want to try a lockstep prefetch that aligns with slice boundaries (i.e., prefetch only full slices) vs current lookahead? That reduces partial-warp loads and seems promising in microbenchmarks.
devin-runtime: yes, include it in matrix. If it helps, we can make it a kernel-level flag (fast path) and enable via rollout.
maria-ml: uploading preliminary heatmap: https://perf.example.com/heat/2001-matrix — initial look: separated_kv reduces p99 by ~30% at batch 16/seq 8192 on A100. fused better at batch 32 but with more variance.
sara-engr: thanks all. Action items: Kai -> patch selector + add bank_conflict metric; Devin -> add canary config & rollback plan; Maria -> full matrix + CSV; I'll coordinate rollout meetings with infra. If anyone hits an urgent regression in canary, @devin-runtime please alert on #incidents.
devin-runtime: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note: archived trace files stored under s3://redwood-perf/traces/2001234567/
kai-profiling: started local bisect to find commit that changed heuristic, it's between 9c4a2e -> b2f9c11. will post small PR once validated.
